- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.6) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.4) — increase forecast by 1–3% for low sentiment days.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price increases — cap forecast growth at 2–4% above prior day unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Allow for mean reversion in 3–5 day horizons — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each day where sentiment is below 0.4 — especially if true outcome shows downward drift.
- If sentiment drops below 0.2 after a spike, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overcorrection lag.
